cases.name: Create a data platform
cases.description:
Objective: Proactively manage inventory health by simulating future aging behavior—not just reacting to what's aged but anticipating what will age.

A. Forward-Looking Aging for New Orders

Mechanism: Use Snowflake to calculate projected aging based on:

o            Six-month average run rate

o            Category-specific velocity

o            Expected order arrival date

Output: Forecasted aging bands (0–30, 31–60, 60+ days) from arrival to depletion

Use Case: Prevent overstocking by visualizing how new orders will age before they even arrive

B. Current Aging Projection for Stock on Hand

Mechanism: Model current inventory depletion based on:

o            Current sales velocity

o            Known demand plan trajectories

Output: Projected date when existing inventory will cross key aging thresholds

Use Case: Enables pre-emptive mitigation for slow movers, such as markdowns or sales pushes

Key Differentiator: Oracle Planning shows current aging. Snowflake adds a predictive layer, making aging a forward-looking risk indicator.

cases.name: Dental - Onboarding Phase 2
cases.account: BUPA - The British United Provident Association Ltd
cases.description:
Bupa Dental Care (BDC) is the last remaining Business Unit within the Bupa Market Unit that has not migrated any data onto the group's central Snowflake platform (Doc). BDC currently operates an isolated data ecosystem — its own SQL-based data warehouse on a separate Microsoft tenancy — which is creating significant barriers to growth, cross-BU data sharing, and delivery of Bupa's connected care and personalised health ambitions under the Savannah strategy.

The existing legacy platform is already struggling to support current workloads and is not fit for purpose for the analytical, operational, or AI/ML use cases BDC wants to pursue. More critically, BDC's inability to access UKI data sets — due to technical and risk constraints caused by this separation — is directly blocking one of its primary near-term revenue growth levers. BDC also holds one of the richest patient interaction data sets in the group (2–4 touchpoints per patient per year), but this commercial and clinical value remains locked while the data sits outside Doc.

BDC's objective is a full migration to Snowflake — not a lift-and-shift, but a ground-up rebuild of their data platform on Doc. This is a key differentiator from other BUs who have partially migrated. The business wants to maintain a federated operating model, retaining its own data engineering, analytics, and reporting capabilities to preserve the agility and speed of delivery the team is known for. Leadership has aligned on an 18-month delivery timeline, targeting a start at the end of Q2 / beginning of Q3 2026 with completion before the end of 2027 to meet the three-year Savannah window.

Funding is being assembled from multiple sources — BDC internal budget, Market Unit SIFT funding (business case being presented to ET imminently), $93K in available Snowflake partner credits, and a potential Microsoft migration funding pot via the Azure Marketplace partnership. An RFP is being prepared to select a delivery partner, with 6–8 suppliers already notified at a high level. Snowflake is actively supporting the process with funding guidance, technical deep dives on requirements and volumetrics, and RFP template documentation.
